title: Quantum States, Measurement, and Precise Language
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: 四つの原文段落と全九つの学習対象を保持し、元の記述問題を英語四択へ変換しました。

passages.text:
Quantum mechanics was developed because classical concepts failed to organize phenomena such as atomic spectra, black-body radiation, and the photoelectric effect. The theory does not merely add randomness to Newtonian trajectories. It represents a physical state by mathematical amplitudes and uses them to calculate probabilities for specified measurement outcomes. The experiment and the question asked determine which probability distribution is relevant.

Superposition is often paraphrased as “a particle is literally in every classical state at once.” That sentence can mislead. A superposed state combines amplitudes and permits interference; it is not the same as an ordinary statistical mixture in which the system secretly occupies one known classical alternative. Measurement produces an outcome according to the theory's rules, while repeated trials reveal the predicted distribution.

The position-momentum uncertainty relation, written ΔxΔp ≥ ℏ/2 for suitable definitions, is also more than instrument imperfection. Position and momentum are represented by noncommuting operators, so a single quantum state cannot make both distributions arbitrarily narrow. A measurement interaction can add disturbance, but disturbance is not the whole logical basis of the relation. Precise vocabulary prevents a useful theorem from becoming a story about clumsy observers.

Quantum effects support transistors, lasers, atomic clocks, magnetic-resonance methods, and emerging quantum information devices. Yet a quantum computer is not automatically faster for every task. Advantage depends on an algorithm, error control, hardware scale, and comparison with the best classical method. The mature lesson is not that quantum theory permits anything. It is that nature follows precise constraints unlike the classical ones we first learned.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Quantum mechanics permits any outcome without mathematical constraints.

options.label: B
options.text: Quantum concepts require precise distinctions among states, amplitudes, outcomes, and comparisons.

options.label: C
options.text: Uncertainty exists only because instruments are poorly built.

options.label: D
options.text: Every quantum algorithm is faster than every classical algorithm.

questions.answer: 正解：B。本文は状態・振幅・一回の測定結果・分布、重ね合わせと混合、擾乱と非可換性、量子優位性の比較条件を区別します。A・C・Dは精密な制約を消しています。

questions.prompt: How does a quantum state differ from a single measurement outcome?

options.label: A
options.text: A state contains mathematical information for probability distributions, whereas an outcome is one value realized in a specified measurement.

options.label: B
options.text: A single outcome always determines the complete quantum state.

options.label: C
options.text: A state is merely the visible reading from one trial.

options.label: D
options.text: An outcome contains every probability distribution for every possible experiment.

questions.answer: 正解：A。状態は指定された測定結果の確率分布を計算する数学的情報を持ち、outcomeは一回の測定で実現した値です。一結果だけで状態全体は決まりません。B～Dは両者を逆転・同一化します。

questions.prompt: Which description is closest to an “ordinary statistical mixture”?

options.label: A
options.text: Classical uncertainty over alternatives without amplitude interference

options.label: B
options.text: A coherent sum of amplitudes with relative phases

options.label: C
options.text: An operator whose order never matters

options.label: D
options.text: A guarantee of one predetermined visible result

questions.answer: 正解：A。通常の統計混合は古典的な候補についての確率的不確実性で、振幅間の干渉を持ちません。Bは重ね合わせ、Cは可換性、Dは混合を決定論へ強めすぎています。

questions.prompt: What observable feature distinguishes a superposition from ignorance about which classical alternative is occupied?

options.label: A
options.text: Interference that depends on relative phases between amplitudes

options.label: B
options.text: The simple addition of classical probabilities with no cross terms

options.label: C
options.text: A guarantee that every trial produces the same outcome

options.label: D
options.text: The absence of any predicted probability distribution

questions.answer: 正解：A。重ね合わせでは相対位相に応じる振幅干渉が現れます。古典混合は候補の確率を足すだけで干渉項を持たないため、Bは混合側の特徴、C・Dは本文の測定規則に反します。

questions.prompt: Why can the position-momentum uncertainty relation not be explained only by imperfect instruments?

options.label: A
options.text: Noncommuting position and momentum operators impose a lower bound on how narrow both distributions can be in one state.

options.label: B
options.text: All instruments necessarily add the same amount of random noise.

options.label: C
options.text: The relation disappears whenever a detector is calibrated.

options.label: D
options.text: The theory contains no mathematical description of position or momentum.

questions.answer: 正解：A。非可換な演算子の構造により、一つの状態で両分布を同時に任意に狭くできません。装置雑音を減らしてもこの状態依存の下限は残り、B～Dはその数学的根拠を誤ります。

questions.prompt: Which statement about measurement and uncertainty is supported by the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Measurement disturbance and operator noncommutativity are identical claims.

options.label: B
options.text: Noncommutativity constrains state distributions even before extra experimental noise is considered.

options.label: C
options.text: Better apparatus can make both spreads exactly zero.

options.label: D
options.text: The observer's consciousness is required by the stated uncertainty relation.

questions.answer: 正解：B。測定相互作用は擾乱を追加し得ますが、不確定性関係の論理的基礎全体ではありません。Aは二概念を同一化し、Cは下限に反し、Dは本文にも式にもありません。

questions.prompt: Which evidence is necessary before claiming a practical quantum advantage?

options.label: A
options.text: A suitable algorithm, controlled errors, adequate hardware scale, and comparison with the best classical method

options.label: B
options.text: Only the presence of qubits in a device

options.label: C
options.text: A comparison with an intentionally weak classical method

options.label: D
options.text: A promise that all tasks will become faster regardless of scale or accuracy

questions.answer: 正解：A。本文は課題に適したアルゴリズム、誤り制御、装置規模、最良の古典手法との公平な比較を条件とします。B～Dはハードウェア名や不公平な比較だけで優位性を断定します。

questions.prompt: Which statement best expresses the idea that strange quantum behavior is not unrestricted?

options.label: A
options.text: Quantum theory predicts unusual behavior under precise rules such as uncertainty bounds and normalized outcome probabilities.

options.label: B
options.text: Any imagined outcome is permitted because quantum mechanics is nonclassical.

options.label: C
options.text: Quantum constraints apply only to old instruments.

options.label: D
options.text: A quantum computer must outperform every classical computer on every problem.

questions.answer: 正解：A。「奇妙であることは無制限を意味しない」という主張で、不確定性下限、測定確率、許される状態変換、課題依存の優位性などの制約があります。B～Dは非古典性を万能性と混同します。

questions.prompt: Which audit question set best tests an advertised quantum-technology advantage?

options.label: A
options.text: What exact task, input size, accuracy, hardware, error treatment, total cost, and optimized classical baseline were used, and was the advantage measured on useful data?

options.label: B
options.text: Does the product use the word quantum often enough in its advertising?

options.label: C
options.text: Can data loading, repeated sampling, failure rates, and scaling assumptions be omitted?

options.label: D
options.text: Is a theoretical possibility sufficient proof of practical speed and economic value?

questions.answer: 正解：A。実用的優位性には課題、規模、精度、装置、誤り、読み込み・反復を含む総費用、最適化した古典基準、実測範囲を明示する必要があります。B～Dは宣伝語や理論可能性を証拠の代わりにします。
